gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: You are ___ a big risk if you invest all your money in one company.
gaps.explanation: take a risk means to do something that might have a bad result.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ a decision next week.
gaps.explanation: make a decision is the fixed collocation; we do not 'do' or 'give' a decision.

gaps.sentence: Can we ___ a phone call before we leave?
gaps.explanation: make a phone call / make a call is the standard collocation.

gaps.sentence: Despite the pressure, the surgeon ___ calm throughout the operation.
gaps.explanation: keep calm (or stay calm) means to remain calm; the past tense is needed here.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.
